package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as Windows executable payload)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware variant, not a package version)
package_info.why_malicious: TinyNuke is a credential and data theft malware distributed via malicious email campaigns. It is designed to steal sensitive information from infected systems, including credentials and financial data, and is delivered as an executable payload disguised as an invoice-themed ZIP file.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon execution of the dropped payload)
execution_context.file_location: Extracted from ZIP attachment, executed as Windows PE file

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The malware, once executed, injects itself into legitimate processes, scans for stored credentials (such as browser passwords), and exfiltrates them to a remote C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects itself into legitimate Windows processes, enumerates credential stores and browser data, then sends the harvested credentials to a remote command-and-control server via HTTP POST, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process injection, credential harvesting, and unauthorized network exfiltration are all hallmarks of malware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal executables, especially those delivered as invoices, should not inject into other processes or access credential stores and exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may perform similar actions in controlled environments.
key_indicators: Process injection into legitimate Windows processes
Enumeration and access of browser credential stores
Outbound HTTP POST requests to untrusted remote servers

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The malware establishes persistence by creating registry run keys or scheduled tasks to ensure execution on system startup.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates registry entries or scheduled tasks to ensure the malware is executed upon system startup, enabling persistent infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing persistence via registry or scheduled tasks is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate invoice-related executables should not modify system startup settings.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software installers create startup entries, but not from unsolicited email attachments.
key_indicators: Creation of registry run keys or scheduled tasks

attack_chain.action: User receives a phishing email with an invoice-themed ZIP attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens ZIP and executes the contained payload.

attack_chain.action: Malicious executable is run, establishing persistence on the system.
Malware injects into legitimate processes, harvests credentials, and exfiltrates data to C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and data.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of unknown PE files from ZIP attachments
Process injection into legitimate Windows processes
Outbound HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains
Creation of registry run keys or scheduled tasks by unknown executables
file_indicators: Dropped PE files with random or misleading names
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to known TinyNuke C2 infrastructure
Unusual network activity immediately after opening invoice attachments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of PE files extracted from ZIP attachments, especially those with invoice-related filenames. Detect process injection attempts and access to browser credential stores by unknown processes. Alert on outbound HTTP POST requests to suspicious or known malicious domains. Watch for unauthorized creation of registry run keys or scheduled tasks by non-whitelisted executables.
